title: Homomorphisms of split tori are Laurent monomials with integer exponents
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $r,s\geq0$ be integers. Let $T_r=\mathbf G_m^r$ and $T_s=\mathbf G_m^s$ be products of the multiplicative group scheme [def-sc-gm-ga, def-sc-group-scheme], with $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}k$ the trivial group. Then there is an isomorphism of abelian groups
$$\mathbf Z^{\{1,\ldots,s\}\times\{1,\ldots,r\}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-grp}}(T_r,T_s),\qquad (m_{ji})\longmapsto\left((x_i)_i\longmapsto\left(\prod_{i=1}^r x_i^{m_{ji}}\right)_{j=1}^s\right).$$
The source has entrywise addition, the target has pointwise multiplication, and the formula holds on $U$-points for every $k$-scheme $U$, with $x_i\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$. The empty product is $1$.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a), printed pp.233–234, fully faithful character anti-equivalence; D(Z)=G_m and finite direct sums carried to products.

proof.text: Put $L_n=\mathbf Z^n$ with its standard basis $b_i$ and $A_n=k[L_n]=\bigoplus_{v\in L_n}ke^v$, $e^ve^w=e^{v+w}$. By [def-sc-gm-ga], $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ with $m^*(t)=t\otimes t$, $\varepsilon(t)=1$, $i^*(t)=t^{-1}$; the monomials $t^m$, $m\in\mathbf Z$, form a $k$-basis [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring], so $t^m\mapsto e^m$ identifies $k[t,t^{-1}]$ with $A_1$ and these maps with $\Delta(e^m)=e^m\otimes e^m$, $\varepsilon(e^m)=1$, $S(e^m)=e^{-m}$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] $n-1$ times gives $T_n\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_1^{\otimes n})$, and the map $A_1^{\otimes n}\to A_n$, $e^{v_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e^{v_n}\mapsto e^{(v_1,\ldots,v_n)}$, of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (2) is a $k$-algebra isomorphism, since it sends the tensor basis bijectively onto the basis $(e^v)_v$. The product group law is componentwise, so $T_n=\operatorname{Spec}A_n$ with $\Delta(e^v)=e^v\otimes e^v$, $\varepsilon(e^v)=1$, $S(e^v)=e^{-v}$ and $e^{(v_i)}$ the function $\prod_ix_i^{v_i}$; for $n=0$ this is $\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a $k$-group morphism $f:T_r\to T_s$ gives a $k$-algebra map $f^*:A_s\to A_r$. The multiplication diagram of [def-sc-group-scheme], read using [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], gives $\Delta_r f^*=(f^*\otimes f^*)\Delta_s$; preservation of the identity gives $\varepsilon_r f^*=\varepsilon_s$. Here the tensor map sends $a\otimes b$ to $f^*(a)\otimes f^*(b)$ by the tensor universal property. Thus each $a_j=f^*(e^{b_j})$ satisfies $\Delta_r(a_j)=a_j\otimes a_j$ and $\varepsilon_r(a_j)=1$.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a), proof of full faithfulness, with Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.6; affine products are Stacks Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-group-algebra-group-like-basis] to $M=L_r$ and each $a_j$. It yields $a_j=e^{v_j}$ with $v_j=(m_{j1},\ldots,m_{jr})\in\mathbf Z^r$. These exponents are unique: if $e^v=e^w$ with $v\ne w$, their coefficients at $v$ would be respectively $1$ and $0$, impossible over a field. Since $f^*$ preserves multiplication and inverses, it sends $e^{\sum_j n_jb_j}$ to $e^{\sum_j n_jv_j}$ for every integer tuple $(n_j)$. By $k$-linearity its value on every finite sum is determined. Thus $f$ determines a unique matrix $(m_{ji})$.

source.place: Lemma 12.4 and Remark 12.6, printed p.232; Theorem 12.9(a), printed p.233.

proof.text: Conversely, given $(m_{ji})$, set $v_j=(m_{ji})_i$ and $h:\mathbf Z^s\to\mathbf Z^r$, $h(n)=\sum_j n_jv_j$. Define $F:A_s\to A_r$ by $F(\sum_n c_ne^n)=\sum_n c_ne^{h(n)}$. The equations $h(n+n')=h(n)+h(n')$ and $h(0)=0$ show directly, by distributing finite sums, that $F$ is a unital $k$-algebra map. On each $e^n$ the equations $\Delta_rF=(F\otimes F)\Delta_s$, $\varepsilon_rF=\varepsilon_s$ and $S_rF=FS_s$ read respectively $e^{h(n)}\otimes e^{h(n)}=e^{h(n)}\otimes e^{h(n)}$, $1=1$ and $e^{-h(n)}=e^{h(-n)}$; extend by linearity. The cited affine product and spectrum identifications therefore make $\operatorname{Spec}F:T_r\to T_s$ a group morphism. Its images of the coordinate generators are $e^{v_j}$. Step 2 and uniqueness of ring maps in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] prove that the two constructions are inverse.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a), construction of the fully faithful map (76); Remark 12.6 for the finite-sum coordinate calculation.

proof.text: Let $U$ be any $k$-scheme and put $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. The natural affine-target bijection [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] identifies a $U$-point of $T_r$ with a $k$-algebra map $\theta:A_r\to R$. Such a map is uniquely specified by units $x_i=\theta(e^{b_i})$: its value on $e^v$ is $\prod_i x_i^{v_i}$, and conversely this formula extended to finite sums is a unital algebra map. Pullback along $f$ is composition $\theta\circ f^*$, so its $j$th unit is $\theta(e^{v_j})=\prod_i x_i^{m_{ji}}$. This proves the asserted formula for all $U$, including nonaffine and nonreduced $U$; naturality follows because restriction of sections commutes with products and inverses.

source.place: Proposition 12.3, functor D(M)(R)=Hom(M,R^times); Lemma 12.4, evaluation character; extension to arbitrary U by Stacks Tag 01I1, lemma-morphism-into-affine.

proof.text: For matrices $M,N$ the product of the resulting maps has $j$th coordinate $\prod_i x_i^{m_{ji}}\prod_i x_i^{n_{ji}}=\prod_i x_i^{m_{ji}+n_{ji}}$, since $R^\times$ is abelian. Thus it is the map of $M+N$ (equality also follows on the universal point $U=T_r$), the zero matrix gives the identity-valued map, and $-M$ gives pointwise inverse. The bijection is an isomorphism of abelian groups. If $s=0$ there are no rows and only the map to the trivial group. If $r=0$, every row is the sole vector of $\mathbf Z^0$ and its coordinate is the empty product $1$, giving only the identity section of $T_s$. These also cover $r=s=0$ and the empty test scheme.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a), isomorphism (76), restricted to free groups; empty direct sums/products in Proposition 12.3.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 12.3, Lemma 12.4, Remark 12.6 and Theorem 12.9(a), printed pp.231–234; explicit finite-free-coordinate specialization, with arbitrary-scheme points via Stacks Tag 01I1.
